title: The Dynamics of the Dark Energy Process
content: In this paper, we show that vacuum self-interaction, with its consequent time-varying curvature, is enough to answer all the outstanding questions of the background evolution of the universe. We define our model in terms of a metric with time-varying curvature, and an energy-momentum tensor that includes the energy density and pressure of the vacuum needed for the self-interaction. The exact 2-parameter solution for the resulting Einsteins’ equations includes formulas for the scaling, the curvature, and the vacuum energy density and pressure valid for the entire evolution of the universe starting from the end of the Planck-era inflation and running right through to the present day. This model shows that so-called dark energy is a dynamic process rather than a built-in property of the vacuum. The solution formulas predict the accelerating expansion of the scaling, the nature and value of the cosmological constant, the observed non-zero present-day value of the vacuum curvature, the so-called vacuum equation-of-state, and the fact that the evolution of the universe is the same everywhere. We also compare the model predictions with FRW predictions. For small redshifts, the predicted cosmological parameters such as the scaling and redshifts, are essentially the same, but for large redshifts, the predictions are quite different, with the FRW model exhibiting hypersensitivity to small changes in the model parameters. We argue that the Hubble tension problem is entirely a large redshift issue whose origin is in large part due to a failure of the FRW model.
